P1.evidence: No setter suffix on the title and no setter referenced on the call; the prospect signed himself up through an advertisement, so the read-back check does not apply in the setter sense. The two-part frame ran with a proper agreement check for once — 'let's dive into it, if that's a call with yourself' / 'Yes, sir. Let's go.' Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: P2b is a striking miss: the rep never asked what this man does for work, and then judged him unsuitable for a $4,000-plus programme. Age arrived only because the prospect said 'I'm going to be 40 next year'; height and weight were never asked. Back and knee tweaks were volunteered and not followed up. The single most relevant fact on the call — a 30 lb loss in six weeks using free content — surfaced at 00:17:15, unprompted, after the prospect had already declined, because P2f was never asked. Diet was named by the prospect as a gap ('I don't really have like a structure to like working out and like meal plans') and never explored.

P3.evidence: The surface half ran well. 'What is it that you're ultimately looking for?' plus the 1-10 physicality scale produced toning, mobility and flexibility, and the concrete limitation — 'not have to worry about ducking and then can't get back up because something's tweaking in my back or my knee.' The ripple question ran but the prospect redirected into the comfort-zone theme and the rep followed that instead of the arenas. P3f never ran at all, and the strongest available material went unused: the prospect volunteered 'I want them to be like, yo, is that your brother?' about his children and the rep did not take a single follow-up on it.

P4.evidence: Two good questions landed the root cause — 'How long would you say you've been comfortable for?' producing eight to nine years, and 'What do you feel like that's cost you so far? I mean, eight years is almost a decade, brother.' The prospect then named the gap himself with unusual clarity: 'I stopped challenging myself... the people that I was surrounded with weren't really challenging me to better myself.' P4f is the decisive miss. This prospect owns the kettlebells and maces, follows two coaches' free content, has bought at least one other online programme and had just lost 30 lb on his own. 'The information isn't the problem, so why can't you stick to it on your own?' is the entire conversation and it was never had.

P5.evidence: P5b ran cleanly and produced the best line of the call — 'But do you want to be okay?' / 'I want to be great.' P5d also ran, 'So are you actually ready to take that step?', drew 'Possibly, yeah', and the rep challenged it well: 'the fact that you said possibly is the reason why you're in the position today.' Neither the two-year projection nor the why-not followed, so the frame was never closed and the challenge had nothing behind it. The comfort-zone and fear sequence ran but the prospect pre-empted it with his own extreme-sports answer and it never converted into commitment.

P6.evidence: No commitment check ran. The earlier 1-10 was about his own physicality, not about belief in the programme, so there is no confidence measure anywhere on this call. P6c was inverted: hesitation surfaced ('Possibly, yeah'), and rather than returning to Phase 5 the rep used it as grounds to disqualify — 'when you said possibly, it doesn't indicate to me that you're actually serious to actually make that step' — and moved to the downsell.

P11.evidence: Both options were declined outright and the prospect ended the call, so no payment or onboarding step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Run pre-emptively as a frame. The comfort-zone question, the Tony Robbins line, the fear question and the responsibility question all ran and produced 'Me.' But the prospect had already dismantled the frame himself — 'I do all type of extreme sports. So I don't really, like when I want to do something, I just do it' — and even supplied the rep's own plane analogy before he could use it. The frame was aimed at a prospect for whom fear was demonstrably not the blocker, and it consumed the middle of an 18-minute call.
No money objection at any point. Price was never questioned, never negotiated and never mentioned by the prospect. He declined on what the offer is, not what it costs.

The most important script gap surfaced anywhere in this batch: the prospect said the advertising promised something the call was not delivering. 'The way that the ad that I clicked on was branded, has, like, I had one idea and the way this is going is another way' and then, in detail, a selected 90-day transformation challenge. There is no scripted play for an advertising-to-offer mismatch — no acknowledgement, no reframe, no explanation of what the ad actually offers. The rep answered 'Sure, man. Sure' and screen-shared the downsell, which confirmed the prospect's suspicion rather than resolving it.

The second known script gap, in its strongest form yet: a cheaper alternative that genuinely worked. He had lost roughly 30 lb in six weeks using Trevor's free Instagram and YouTube routines, another coach's free movements and his own gym time. Objection C assumes the blocker is capacity to pay; here the blocker is that the free version is visibly working. It surfaced only after the decline because P2f and P4f were both skipped, so the rep never had the chance to address it.

notes: A two-year warm follower who owns the equipment, uses the content daily and had just lost 30 lb was lost in eighteen minutes without anyone asking what he does for work, what he currently weighs, what results he is getting, or a single question about money. He told the rep twice that the advertising had set a different expectation and got no engagement either time. The rep instead spent the middle of the call on a fear frame aimed at a man who does extreme sports, then used a soft answer to a readiness question as grounds to route him to the $200 product. Coach two things: qualify before disqualifying, and build an answer for the 90-day-challenge expectation that this advertising is evidently creating.
